subject: Cloud Computing
title: PaaS Lock-In Risks
description: Learn PaaS Lock-In Risks in one minute.

hook.text: You built your entire app on a PaaS. Now the provider raises prices 300%. Moving is nearly impossible.

buildup.text: PaaS simplifies by hiding infrastructure. But that means your app depends on proprietary platform features.

discovery.text: Custom APIs, build systems, and integrations tie you to one provider. Migration means rewriting code.

twist.text: Some teams accept lock-in willingly. The speed of shipping outweighs the risk of vendor dependency.

climax.text: The best protection is building on open standards — containers, SQL, standard protocols.

punchline.text: PaaS is fast to adopt. It can be painful to leave.

quiz.question: What causes PaaS lock-in?
options: Dependence on proprietary platform features that don't exist elsewhere
PaaS providers legally prevent customers from leaving
Applications deployed on PaaS cannot be backed up

details.summary: PaaS lock-in occurs when applications become dependent on provider-specific APIs, services, or configurations that make migration difficult and expensive. The more deeply integrated with a platform, the higher the switching cost.
details.whyItMatters: Lock-in surrenders negotiating leverage and limits flexibility. Understanding lock-in risks helps teams make deliberate trade-offs between convenience and portability.
takeaways: Deep platform integration increases switching costs
Containers and open standards reduce lock-in risk

faq.question: How can you minimize PaaS lock-in?
faq.answer: Use containers for portability, prefer open-source databases over proprietary ones, abstract provider-specific services behind interfaces, and avoid using more than a few provider-unique services per application. The goal is deliberate adoption, not accidental dependency.

faq.question: Is some lock-in acceptable?
faq.answer: Yes. Managed services that save significant engineering time are often worth the lock-in trade-off. The key is making the choice deliberately, understanding the migration cost, and ensuring the vendor provides competitive pricing without exploiting your dependency.
